subject: Reconciliation: unexpected usage spike — credits & postmortem
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@saasco.com>
Cc: SaaSCo Billing <billing@saasco.com>
Date: 2026-07-28T08:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected usage spike — immediate reconciliation plan

Alyssa — I wanted to reach out as soon as we confirmed the scope of an internal incident that inflated token counts on your account earlier this morning. Short version: a routing race in our ingress dedupe layer caused certain requests to be replayed and counted twice between 07:00–08:45 UTC.

What we're doing now:
- We've paused the offending pipeline and deployed a fix.
- Applied a provisional credit for the immediately visible duplicate usage (see attached interim CSV).
- My team is preparing a full postmortem and a per-project breakdown by EOD tomorrow.

I know this impacts your month-end reconciliation. I'm available for a quick 20–30 minute call today to walk through the numbers and make sure we cover every project you need line-by-line. Are you free 3pm UTC / 11am ET?

Apologies for the disruption — we'll make this right.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: provisional_reconciliation_saasco_20260728.csv (csv)
From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@saasco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike — immediate reconciliation plan

Ben — thanks for the quick note. Can you confirm:
1) Which projects/keys were affected? We bill individual product teams separately.
2) Exact timeframe for the duplicate counts (timezone converted to ET would help).
3) Is the provisional credit already visible on our account or will it appear on the next invoice?

We also need the raw audit csv showing request ids so our finance team can reconcile with our internal logs. If you can share that and the HubSpot ticket id I can route it to procurement.

Alyssa Greene
Head of Procurement, SaaSCo
alyssa.greene@saasco.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T11:30:00Z
Subject: Internal: incident summary & numbers for SaaSCo

Internal summary for customer-facing response (do not change without sync):
Root cause: a race in the ingress deduplication TTL check allowed duplicate request envelopes to be enqueued to the serving fabric during a brief autoscaling event. When the worker processing order diverged across replicas we observed request replays that bypassed the token-count guard.

Impact window: 2026-07-28 07:00:12 UTC -> 2026-07-28 08:45:23 UTC
Estimated scope for SaaSCo: ~1.2 billion tokens counted twice (±6%). Affected model variants: rdx-7b and rdx-13b (inferred from route logs).
Mitigation: rolled back the dedupe regression at 08:46 UTC, applied hotfix to ingress ordering, added an emergency monitoring alert to detect >10% per-route token variance relative to 15min rolling baseline.
Remediation plan:
- Credit schedule: provisional credit applied now; final reconciliation and per-project CSV by 2026-07-29 18:00 UTC.
- Permanent fix: kernel merged, will be included in next runtime release; added post-deploy canary test.

Attachments: incident_postmortem.pdf (pdf)

Let me know if you want the full query list (request ids) attached — that will require a sanitized delivery (PII scrubbed).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability
monica.patel@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@saasco.com>
Cc: SaaSCo Billing <billing@saasco.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike — immediate reconciliation plan

Alyssa — quick follow-up with attachments and concrete next steps.

What we attached:
- saasco_credit_schedule.csv: shows provisional credit (line-level) applied today and a placeholder for the final adjustment after reconciliation.
- incident_postmortem.pdf: short technical summary and timeline.

Where credit appears: provisional credit applied to your account as a negative balance; it will reduce your next invoice but we can also apply an immediate invoice-level adjustment if you prefer (let me know).

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll send a reconciled per-project CSV by 2026-07-29 18:00 UTC.
2) Offer a one-time invoice adjustment if you need it now — finance is standing by.
3) Schedule a 30-minute call to review the breakdown and to confirm SLA credit (if eligible).

Proposed call times (ET): 11:00 today, 16:00 today, or 10:00 tomorrow. Which works best?

Thanks again for your patience. We take this seriously and have already introduced monitoring and code fixes to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Ben
From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@saasco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: SaaSCo Billing <billing@saasco.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike — immediate reconciliation plan

Ben — thanks. We can take the 10:00 tomorrow (ET) slot. A couple of items to prepare for the call:
- Per-project breakdown (by API key) with total duplicate tokens per project.
- Raw request ids and timestamps (sanitized) if possible so our infra team can correlate.
- Clarify whether this incident qualifies for SLA service credit and, if so, the formula you’ll use.

Also confirm whether the provisional credit is visible now in the billing portal (we still see the charge pending today). If the provisional credit is not yet visible, please escalate finance to apply an immediate invoice-level adjustment.

Alyssa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@saasco.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T10:00:00Z
Subject: Final postmortem & reconciliation link — SaaSCo incident

Alyssa — attaching the finalized postmortem and the reconciliation package. Links below:
- Final postmortem (sanitized PDF): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2b3Postmortem
- Reconciliation CSVs (per-project and per-api-key) included in the folder.
- HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/67890

Summary of outcome:
- Root cause: ingress dedupe race during autoscale event.
- Total duplicate tokens: 1.18B for SaaSCo.
- Credits applied: immediate provisional credit issued 2026-07-28; final credit posted 2026-07-30 and reflected on your account as a negative invoice for the July billing period.
- SLA credit: you qualify under our SLA window; finance will apply a separate SLA credit per contractual terms, visible as a line item on your August invoice.

If you’d like the raw request ids for cross-correlation we can provide a sanitized export under an NDA — let us know and we’ll route the data transfer through your security contact.

Thanks for working with us on this. I can join the call or hand off to Ben depending on what you prefer.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
